**Setup.** With m* = 0.067 m₀, ħ²/2m* = 0.5687 eV·nm². Let k = √(E/0.5687), κ = √((0.30−E)/0.5687) (nm⁻¹), well width a = 4 nm, barrier width d = b = 1.5 nm.

**Resonance condition.** For a symmetric structure T = 1 when the even and odd interior solutions satisfy λ_e·λ_o = −k² at the outer edge (even/odd outside waves in quadrature). Propagating through the finite outer barrier, this fixes the logarithmic derivative μ of the resonant well solution at the inner edge of the outer barrier (instead of −κ for infinitely thick barriers). In the central barrier the even/odd solutions are cosh/sinh, so the well solution cos(k(x−b/2)+φ) has tan φ_e = −(κ/k)tanh(κb/2), tan φ_o = −(κ/k)coth(κb/2), and the peak condition is

ka = arctan(−μ/k) + arctan[(κ/k)·tanh or coth(κb/2)].

**Even (lower) peak:** iterating, near E ≈ 0.087 eV (k ≈ 0.391, κ ≈ 0.612, tanh(κb/2) ≈ 0.429), the finite-barrier correction gives μ_e ≈ −0.572 (vs −κ = −0.612). Solving: E₁ ≈ 86.9 meV (vs ≈ 88.7 meV for infinitely thick outer barriers).

**Odd (upper) peak:** near E ≈ 0.141 eV (k ≈ 0.499, κ ≈ 0.528, coth(κb/2) ≈ 2.66), μ_o ≈ −0.478 (vs −κ = −0.528). Solving: E₂ ≈ 141.3 meV (vs ≈ 145.6 meV for infinitely thick outer barriers).

(For reference, an isolated 4 nm well has its level at ≈115.5 meV; the 1.5 nm central barrier splits it into the symmetric/antisymmetric pair.)

**Splitting:** ΔE ≈ 141.3 − 86.9 ≈ 54 meV.
